architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Using at least two independent preparations, accept the low-drift acrylic-only result if every repeat has SI_15_60 < 4.04%, the arithmetic mean is < 4.04%, and the repeat range is <= 2.00 percentage points. The 4.04% threshold is half the nominal H-CORE prediction of 9.51% × 0.85 = 8.08%. This supports H-RESIN over H-CORE and, because TK100 is absent, falsifies H-DUAL's requirement for a minor tackifier to reach the low-drift regime.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C39 is acrylic-resin-modified chemistry outside the previously measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI thermal-response family. However, the selected primary observable is measured directly in S1C39 and does not depend on any rheological regularity previously measured in the same chemistry family, nor on shared-shape transfer or reconstruction. The resulting claim is therefore limited to formulation-level 120 C drift in S1C39 and cannot establish a molecular mechanism or transferable temperature-response shape.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: For repeats with a range <= 2.00 percentage points: a mean SI_15_60 >= 8.08% falsifies H-RESIN for S1C39; a mean < 6.08% is more than the registered 2.00 percentage-point resolution below the 8.08% linear-dilution prediction and falsifies H-CORE; and a mean < 4.04% additionally falsifies H-DUAL because the acrylic-only candidate reached the registered low-drift regime. A mean from 4.04% to < 6.08% falsifies H-CORE but supports neither H-RESIN nor H-DUAL. A mean from 6.08% to < 8.08% does not cleanly falsify any registered hypothesis. A repeat range > 2.00 percentage points is not adjudicated as hypothesis falsification because realization-state ambiguity exceeds the declared resolution.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If H-RESIN is falsified by mean SI_15_60 >= 8.08%, run the dual-axis S1C41 formulation under M-HOLD-120 to test whether adding the 5 wt% minor-tackifier axis produces the low-drift regime predicted by H-DUAL. If the repeat range exceeds 2.00 percentage points instead, first run a controlled repeatability/state-control study on S1C39 before interpreting formulation effects.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of directly measured SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C; individual repeat values and their percentage-point range are retained.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C39::M-HOLD-120 is an admissible, direct rheological probe of the declared failure mode and uniquely tests whether acrylic modification alone can produce superlinear drift suppression. It avoids unsupported shared-shape transfer and provides greater registered-hypothesis discrimination than the proposed dual-axis card, while restricting conclusions to formulation-level rheology.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer and deterministic top-ranked dual-axis set. The Proposer's S1C41 experiment directly tests mitigation but cannot meet H-DUAL's registered acrylic-only falsification condition, leaving H-RESIN and H-DUAL entangled. S1C39 uses the same admissible direct hold measurement while removing TK100, so a low-drift result can distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL. This hypothesis-separation gain justifies departing from the stable VOI ranking, whose stability is not a probability of scientific correctness.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Only E1 and E5 have original 120 C hold trajectories, each from one run, and there is no local resin-modified hold result. External evidence supports only a coarse acrylic-modifier region, while the runtime external-prior queries returned no additional entries.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The direct drift measurement avoids cross-chemistry thermal-shape extrapolation, but interpretation of the nominal 8.08% H-CORE benchmark assumes the stated 0.85 reactive mass fraction. Unknown AC1920 reactive functionality could alter the true reactive fraction or NCO:OH balance, so material functionality should be verified before applying the benchmark beyond this preregistered nominal comparison.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 directly observes the endpoint ratio without fitting or thermal extrapolation. The registered matched-window discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points; at least two independent repeats are required, and a repeat range above 2.00 points prevents threshold adjudication.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: The E2 core exhibited 2.80-3.57× between-preparation viscosity-scale spread. Controlled and fully recorded preparation histories are therefore required, and the 15-minute viscosity level must be retained alongside relative drift even though it is not the primary observable.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local thermal-response regularities were measured in the original reactive PUR/prepolymer family represented by E1–E3, with the E1 +P chemical perturbation treated as a separate compatibility check. An E2-core experiment containing acrylic-like or minor tackifier-like modifiers changes the measured chemistry support; it must not inherit the shared thermal-response regularity unless the chemistry audit and candidate-specific applicability assessment establish that it remains in-domain.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive and formulation-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged 120 °C melt residence (thermal-hold drift).
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold measured SI_15_60 = 0.5154 (51.54% viscosity growth) and SI_15_90 = 0.9308 (93.08%) at 120 °C, versus 9.51% and 16.85%, respectively, for E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 °C hold trajectories, each represented by one run with four measurements over 15–90 min. In contrast, temperature response was measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 °C across multiple formulations and realizations, and realized viscosity-level variability was directly characterized for three E2 runs, although that variability is large.
measurement_requirements: Use the direct M-HOLD-120 protocol: hold at 120 °C, measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage.
Run at least two independent preparations under controlled and recorded process histories so that formulation-dependent drift is not confounded with realization state.

Determine the candidate reactive mass fraction and prospectively calculate the H-CORE benchmark as 9.51% × phi_r; use the registered 2 percentage-point matched-window resolution when judging agreement.

Test H-RESIN only by the preregistered criterion that measured drift is below half of the linear-dilution benchmark; values near the benchmark support H-CORE, while intermediate values do not cleanly separate the hypotheses.
Retain the measured 15 min viscosity level alongside relative drift so that a low drift result is not confused with an uncontrolled or impractical realized viscosity state.
If a shared temperature-response shape or one-point calibration is used in an experiment card, first establish candidate-specific chemistry applicability; otherwise require a direct 80–130 °C sweep.
planner.scientific_question: For an E2-core resin-modified candidate, is the measured 15–60 min viscosity drift at 120 °C consistent with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, E1_drift × reactive mass fraction, or is it less than half that prediction as required by H-RESIN superlinear suppression?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is resin-modified chemistry outside the family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured. However, M-HOLD-120 directly observes thermal-hold drift and does not infer it from that shared shape, so the binding audit marks this card admissible. Its composition is also inside the externally supported intervention regions: 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier is within the 15-25 wt% broad region and conservative 15-20 wt% initial band, while 5 wt% minor tackifier lies in the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster.
hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL; both predict low drift for this dual-axis composition

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, it is below half the 7.61% H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for phi_r = 0.80. This falsifies H-CORE at the registered separation threshold and supports superlinear resin-associated suppression. The result is compatible with both H-RESIN and H-DUAL and cannot distinguish them.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified for this candidate. Agreement with 7.61% within the 2 percentage-point resolution supports H-CORE; a value materially above that range would reject simple superlinear suppression without cleanly supporting the linear-dilution model. Because the candidate contains tackifier, this outcome does not satisfy H-DUAL's registered acrylic-only falsification condition.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to below 7.61% indicates suppression relative to the linear benchmark but not enough to meet the preregistered H-RESIN criterion. It would not cleanly select H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL and would motivate an acrylic-only hold to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold across at least two independent preparations

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: VOI-tied and equally direct, but its 17.5 wt% acrylic loading creates a larger chemistry departure than S1C41 without adding hypothesis separation.
VOI-tied and located at a directly supported 20 wt% acrylic anchor, but it uses more modifier than necessary for the same discrimination.
VOI-tied but carries 22.5 wt% acrylic, increasing intervention burden without improving directness, support class, or hypothesis-pair separation.
VOI-tied and externally supported at 25 wt% acrylic, but it is the largest chemistry perturbation in the tied set and lies outside the conservative 15-20 wt% initial-test band.
It provides the same direct discrimination, but 7.5 wt% TK100 lies above the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.
It directly addresses realization-state variability but does not separate any registered formulation-mechanism hypotheses and has lower decision relevance to thermal-hold drift.
It measures a fitted temperature-response descriptor rather than the declared failure mode, separates no registered hypotheses, and has lower decision relevance and interpretability.

proposer.reasoning: The selected card has the top VOI score of 0.6925, directly measures the least-resolved and decision-critical isothermal drift coordinate, and separates two of three registered hypothesis pairs without relying on an unverified cross-chemistry thermal-shape transfer. Controlled process histories, at least two independent preparations, and retention of the 15-minute viscosity level are necessary because the E2 core showed large realization variability. Within the genuine five-way tie, S1C41 is preferred by the registered minimum-sufficient-intervention policy.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI components and separate the same two hypothesis pairs. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden, 15 wt% AC1920 plus 5 wt% TK100, while remaining within both supported regions and the conservative acrylic initial-test band. It therefore makes the smallest justified departure from the characterized reactive-core chemistry without sacrificing discrimination or directness.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the dual-axis S1C41::M-HOLD-120 test with the acrylic-only S1C39::M-HOLD-120 test. Both use the direct, admissible hold observable, but S1C39 removes the tackifier axis and directly tests H-DUAL's registered acrylic-only condition. Before applying an H-CORE benchmark, verify AC1920 reactive functionality and recalculate the true reactive mass fraction and NCO:OH balance if necessary; also preregister repeat aggregation and discordance rules.
residual_decision_risk: S1C39 remains resin-modified chemistry outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI thermal-response support, although M-HOLD-120 directly measures drift and does not require shared-shape transfer.
Unknown AC1920 reactive functionality could invalidate a benchmark based only on nominal reactive-core mass fraction.
Large E2 realization variability can confound formulation effects unless independent preparations have controlled and recorded process histories.
At least two repeats are required, but an explicit aggregation and discordant-repeat rule must be preregistered.
Bulk viscosity drift can establish phenomenological suppression but cannot identify a molecular reduced-encounter-frequency mechanism.
The exact candidate-grid provenance lacks a contemporaneous freeze artifact, limiting independent verification of the asserted outcome-blind construction.
Decision behavior outside the tested 0.5-to-1.5 weight-scaling range is unknown.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The deterministic score credits S1C41 with separating H-CORE from H-DUAL, but its dual-axis composition cannot satisfy H-DUAL's registered acrylic-only falsification condition. Every member of the tied top set retains this same entanglement. The score therefore overstates practical hypothesis coverage. S1C39::M-HOLD-120 is the selectable 15 wt% acrylic-only direct-hold experiment and can distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL: low drift without TK100 falsifies H-DUAL, whereas drift near the linear-dilution prediction is compatible with H-DUAL and argues against H-RESIN. This scientifically relevant distinction justifies departing from the deterministic top set.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is one of five experiments in the base tied top set. The tied top set remained unchanged in all 25 tested one-term perturbations, with every weight scaled from 0.5 to 1.5; no recommendation_flip_boundary was observed for any term. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.004583. Thus no tested weighting, defensible or otherwise, changes the ranking, although behavior beyond the tested scaling range is unknown.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry support, but the primary observable remains valid because M-HOLD-120 measures SI_15_60 directly in the candidate and does not reuse the unmodified-family thermal-response shape. No direct sweep is required for this drift observable. A candidate-specific M-SWEEP would be required before using the shared temperature-response shape or a one-point M-ANCHOR reconstruction in this resin-modified family.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The direct 15- and 60-minute viscosity measurements can produce SI_15_60 values below 3.80% or at or above 7.61%, so the stated H-CORE and H-RESIN criteria are attainable. The protocol should add an explicit repeat-level aggregation rule for discordant results. H-DUAL is not falsifiable in this experiment because its registered criterion requires an acrylic-only composition.
leakage_findings: No target hold result or explicit outcome-derived label is visible in the proposal.

The exact grid and refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment, and no contemporaneous repository freeze artifact is available; the payload asserts outcome exclusion, but that prospective provenance cannot be independently verified from the supplied record.
The planned rheology can support phenomenological superlinear suppression but cannot establish the stated reduced-encounter-frequency mechanism.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The claimed discrimination score of two out of three hypothesis pairs overstates practical hypothesis separation; H-DUAL remains non-falsifiable in this experiment and H-RESIN remains entangled with it.
objections.objection: The proposal lists "H-CORE vs H-DUAL" under hypotheses_separated, but S1C41 contains both 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100, whereas the registered falsification condition for H-DUAL requires an acrylic-only composition to reach the low-drift regime without minor tackifier. The proposer itself states that no outcome on this tackifier-containing candidate satisfies that H-DUAL falsification condition. Thus this experiment separates H-CORE from the shared low-drift prediction of H-RESIN/H-DUAL, but it cannot adjudicate H-DUAL as a registered hypothesis. The H-CORE versus H-RESIN numerical predictions, 7.608% versus below 3.804%, differ by 3.804 percentage points and therefore do exceed the declared 2.0 percentage-point resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: An intermediate result could be incorrectly reported as wholly non-discriminating rather than as evidence against H-CORE without positive support for H-RESIN.
objections.objection: The outcome interpretation understates the registered H-CORE falsification region. With an H-CORE prediction of 7.608% and a 2.0 percentage-point resolution, drift substantially below approximately 5.608% is beyond resolution from H-CORE, not only drift below the 3.80% H-RESIN threshold. Results from 3.80% to about 5.61% would fail to support H-RESIN but could still falsify H-CORE under its registered criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low drift result would support only a formulation-level effect of the combined intervention. It would not establish which modifier axis caused suppression, would not establish the H-DUAL specialization mechanism, and could invalidate the 7.61% linear-dilution benchmark if either modifier is reactive.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is set to 15 wt% and TK100 to 5 wt%, while the E2 reactive core is reduced to phi_r = 0.80. Consequently, any change in SI_15_60 cannot be attributed separately to the acrylic-like modifier, the minor tackifier-like modifier, their interaction, or reactive-core dilution. In addition, the payload states that true stoichiometry must be recalculated if a modifier contributes OH or another NCO-reactive group, but the proposal uses phi_r = 0.80 and the 7.61% benchmark without documenting verified modifier functionality.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The observable itself remains interpretable, but conflicting repeats could make the threshold adjudication ambiguous.
objections.objection: No primary-observable defect is evident. M-HOLD-120 directly calculates SI_15_60 from measured viscosities at 15 and 60 minutes; it requires no fitted thermal-response model, extrapolation, or imputation. However, the protocol does not specify how two potentially discordant repeat values are combined or how repeat uncertainty is compared with the 2.0 percentage-point resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No cross-chemistry shape-transfer claim is needed for SI_15_60. A direct M-SWEEP would be required only before using the unmodified-family temperature-response shape for reconstruction or state transfer in S1C41.
objections.objection: The proposed primary observable does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape measured in unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI material. Although S1C41 is outside that chemistry family, M-HOLD-120 directly measures drift in S1C41 and is admissible under the binding audit. The proposal correctly avoids the inadmissible one-point M-ANCHOR reconstruction for this modified chemistry.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment can falsify H-RESIN or H-CORE in principle, but discordant repeats may lack a preregistered decision rule, and H-DUAL cannot be falsified by this protocol.
objections.objection: The numerical H-RESIN and H-CORE criteria are physically attainable by the specified direct hold measurement: SI_15_60 can be at or above 7.61% or below 3.80%. However, "across at least two repeats" is operationally defined only for the low-drift acceptance statement; the protocol does not say whether H-RESIN is falsified when one repeat is at or above 7.61% and another is below it. H-DUAL's acrylic-only falsification condition cannot be met by S1C41 under any measured outcome.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A phenomenological drift result could be overinterpreted as evidence for a specific concentration or encounter-frequency mechanism, and the prospective status of the exact candidate construction would rest on an asserted rather than independently frozen provenance record.
objections.objection: No direct use of an unmeasured S1C41 outcome is visible. Nevertheless, the H-RESIN statement attributes suppression to reduced effective concentration and encounter frequency, while M-HOLD-120 measures only bulk viscosity drift. This rheological measurement can establish superlinear suppression relative to the dilution benchmark but cannot establish that particular underlying mechanism. The payload also notes that the current exact grid and refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment; although it explicitly states that held-out coordinates and outcomes were excluded, the missing contemporaneous freeze artifact limits independent verification of that no-leakage claim.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace or augment the dual-axis-only test with a selectable acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 comparison under the same 120 C, 15-60 minute window and controlled preparation protocol. This is required to test H-DUAL's registered falsification condition. Before calculating the H-CORE benchmark, verify AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality from material specifications and recalculate true reactive mass fraction and NCO:OH if necessary. Also preregister how replicate SI_15_60 values and discordant repeats will be adjudicated.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The experiment overclaims hypothesis coverage: because S1C41 activates both AC1920 and TK100, no possible result can meet H-DUAL's registered acrylic-only falsification condition, and the individual modifier effects and their interaction remain confounded. The claimed "H-CORE vs H-DUAL" separation is therefore not a practical adjudication of H-DUAL.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded before any candidate or experiment ranking; it establishes the chemistry provenance, state-shift evidence, hold contrast, and valid scope of the local rheological regularities.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
